newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-C&W wins 67 pct of Germany with RWE.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-C&W wins 67 pct of Germany with RWE.

text.p: British telecom operator Cable and Wireless said on Wednesday that it would have access to about two thirds of German consumers now that energy giant RWE had joined its alliance with VEBA.

"If you combine what Veba have and what RWE have now, the combined network gives us access to something like 67 percent of the German population," Stephen Pettit, Cable & Wireless' executive director, Europe and mobile, told Reuters.
RWE said earlier on Wednesday that it was pulling out of an alliance with C&W's main British competitor, British Telecommunications, and Germany's Viag.
Pettit said talks with RWE, whose alliance with BT broke down because of divergent views about the importance of mobile telephones in the German market, had been going on for some weeks.

"The idea of RWE coming in with their fibre optic cable associated with their electicity pylons has given us not only a partner to share the infrastructure investment -- but brings with them a very significant capability," he said.
The C&W, Veba alliance announced the final deal after the London market closed on Wednesday. Pettit denied he felt any glee that RWE had ruptured its links with BT.
"This is not about glee. This is about making sure we have the strongest possible company to win the long-term business. The fact that RWE have decided to join us is great news," he said.
Cable and Wireless said the deal would boost earnings, cash and its balance sheet.

Under the deal, two separate companies have been set up -- Servco, a services company, including mobile and satellite interests; and Netco, a network company including Veba's transport network and RWE's fixed network activities.
Veba is taking a 40 percent shareholding of the new grouping, with RWE taking about 38 percent and Cable and Wireless about 22 percent.
